explanations: terra: إِيَّاكَ نَعْبُدُ وَإِيَّاكَ نَسْتَعِينُ fronts the sole object of worship and help, clarifying the same exclusivity the section draws from fronting وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ.
terra: Whoever submits his face to God while doing good has his reward with his Lord; orientation, action, and divine recompense appear in one formulation.

luna: The section's root ر غ ب in the sense of turning away appears in وَمَن يَرْغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبْرَٰهِـۧمَ; the verse marks rejection of Abraham's way as the contrary orientation. | terra: مَن يَرْغَبُ عَن مِّلَّةِ إِبْرَاهِيمَ uses رغب with عَنْ for turning away, the exact grammatical reversal of the source section's رغب with إِلَىٰ.
terra: When his Lord says “Submit,” Abraham says he submits to the Lord of the worlds; this is the positive response immediately following 2:130's question about turning away from Abraham's way.
terra: Each community has a direction toward which it turns, followed by the command to race in good works and the promise that God will gather all; direction is tested by action and final gathering.
terra: The Ramadan ruling says to complete the prescribed number and then magnify God for His guidance, directly pairing completion with a Godward act rather than vacancy.

terra: Upon pouring forth from Arafat, pilgrims are told to remember God at the sacred place; the transition from a completed movement into remembrance begins the ritual sequence continued in 2:199-200.
terra: Pilgrims are told to depart where the people depart and then seek God's forgiveness, another completed movement followed by a deliberately Godward act before 2:200's completed rites.

luna: After completing the pilgrimage rites, the verse commands remembrance of Allah; it directly matches the section's sequence of finishing one act and turning to the Lord. | terra: After completing the rites, pilgrims must remember God intensely; the same ayah contrasts that directed remembrance with a person whose request stops at “give us in this world.”

luna: After the Hajj remembrance in 2:200, this prayer asks for good in this world and the next; it specifies what a desire directed to God may seek. | terra: Immediately after 2:200's person who asks only for this world, this speaker addresses “our Lord” for good in both this world and the Hereafter, correcting desire without denying earthly good.

luna: The Hajj passage says أُو۟لَٰٓئِكَ لَهُمْ نَصِيبٌ مِّمَّا كَسَبُوا۟; the section's root ن ص ب also occurs here in the distinct sense of an allotted share, joined to what people earn. | terra: Those who make the balanced request of 2:201 have a share of what they earned, joining Godward asking to accountable human acquisition; its force depends on the preceding prayer.
luna: The Hajj scene continues with وَٱذْكُرُوا۟ ٱللَّهَ فِىٓ أَيَّامٍ مَّعْدُودَٰتٍ, carrying remembrance beyond the completed rites into the following days.
terra: A person gives up his very self seeking God's pleasure, making arduous action the embodied form of exclusively directed desire.

luna: The section's dictionary sense of ن ص ب includes setting oneself upright; قُومُوا لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ gives the related posture of standing devoutly for Allah. | terra: وَقُومُوا۟ لِلَّهِ قَٰنِتِينَ commands believers to stand devoutly for God, directly joining upright posture to its intended recipient.

terra: Facing battle, the believers ask their Lord to “pour out” (أَفْرِغْ) patience upon them and make their feet firm; the different ف ر غ sense still joins divine address, endurance, and upright steadiness.
terra: Those who spend their wealth seeking God's pleasure and inner firmness are compared to a garden yielding multiplied produce; direction, work, and abundant return are concretely connected.

luna: This charity verse says spending is for oneself and only ابتغاء وجه الله; its promise of repayment connects work for others to a reward sought from Allah. | terra: Whatever good believers spend is to be for seeking God's face and will be repaid in full, linking a concrete act, its exclusive intention, and the giver's return.
terra: A catalog of desired people, treasure, animals, and fields is identified as worldly enjoyment, a concrete expansion of the section's “wide desire” to acquire the world.
terra: Against 3:14's desired possessions, the Prophet asks whether he should announce something better: lasting gardens, purity, and pleasure with their Lord.
terra: Whoever desires worldly reward receives from it and whoever desires Hereafter reward receives from it; the desired recompense distinguishes two orientations within mortal action.

luna: After Uhud, the verse distinguishes among those who want worldly gain and those who want the Hereafter; it shows effort can be aimed in opposite directions. | terra: During a demanding collective charge, some desired the world and others the Hereafter; the ayah shows desire's direction splitting people within the same work.

luna: Its phrase يَذْكُرُونَ ٱللَّهَ قِيَٰمًا وَقُعُودًا وَعَلَىٰ جُنُوبِهِمْ repeats the standing, sitting, and reclining remembrance named in 4:103, extending the section's all-posture turn to God. | terra: Remembering God standing, sitting, and on one's sides shows devotion continuing through every bodily state, closely echoing 4:103 though it lacks that ayah's “after completion” transition.

luna: God promises not to waste any worker’s work, then names migration, expulsion, suffering, and struggle for His cause; it is the positive counterpart to labor that comes to nothing. | terra: The Lord answers the callers that He never lets any worker's work be lost, then names migration, expulsion, suffering, and fighting before promising reward from Himself.

luna: After prayer is completed, remember Allah standing, sitting, and lying on your sides; the verse makes remembrance the next act and keeps it through every posture. | terra: When prayer has been completed, believers are to remember God standing, sitting, and lying down; the explicit “when you have finished ... then” sequence closely matches the source section's completion followed by renewed Godward action.
terra: Private counsel gains great reward when its charity, recognized good, or reconciliation is done seeking God's pleasure; the intended recipient determines the worth of practical work.
terra: The best religious course is to submit one's face to God while doing good and following Abraham, joining Godward orientation with active excellence.

terra: تَرْغَبُونَ أَن تَنكِحُوهُنَّ lacks the preposition that elsewhere tells whether رغبة is toward or away from the orphan women; that grammatical ambiguity specifically illuminates the section's insistence that فِي/إِلَى and عَنْ reverse the verb's direction.
terra: Anyone desiring worldly reward is reminded that both worldly and Hereafter reward are with God, redirecting desire from one limited gift to the Giver who possesses both.

luna: The section's root ن ص ب describes setting upright; this verse forbids meat sacrificed عَلَى ٱلنُّصُب, setting the erect cult stones against the section's prayer and sacrifice directed to the Lord. | terra: Animals sacrificed upon erected stone altars (ٱلنُّصُبِ) are forbidden, sharply contrasting with 108:2's sacrifice expressly performed for one's Lord.
terra: Believers must be mindful of God, seek a means toward Him, and strive in His way; direction toward God and strenuous activity are expressly combined.
terra: Believers are told to race in good works and that all will return to God, coupling purposeful activity with the common destination that explains its direction.

luna: The same section root ن ص ب appears as ٱلْأَنصَاب, erected stones for idolatrous rites; this marks a concrete boundary against directing worship anywhere but the Lord. | terra: The erected stones or altars (ٱلْأَنصَابُ) are called satanic filth to avoid; this concrete ن ص ب object reverses the section's uprightness by giving cultic direction to something other than the Lord.
terra: Those who call their Lord morning and evening “desiring His face” embody sustained, exclusively directed desire, and the Prophet is commanded not to drive them away.
terra: Abraham turns his face toward the Creator of heavens and earth as an upright monotheist and rejects association, a vivid enacted counterpart to directing desire only toward the Lord.

luna: The section names ش ر ح from the opening of the breast; this verse uses يَشْرَحْ صَدْرَهُ لِلْإِسْلَٰمِ for a breast opened to Islam, specifying a Godward openness. | terra: God opens a breast to Islam for the one He wills to guide, while misdirection makes it constricted as though climbing upward; the root ش ر ح marks a divinely given capacity whose direction is decisive.

luna: The Prophet says his prayer, sacrifice, life, and death are for Allah, Lord of the worlds; this gives the section’s direction toward the Lord a whole-life form. | terra: The Prophet declares that his prayer, sacrifice, life, and death are for God, Lord of the worlds, making every act and the whole life cycle share one direction.

luna: The next verse adds that Allah has no partner and that this was commanded, sharpening the exclusivity stated in 6:162. | terra: “No partner has He” makes the exclusivity of 6:162 explicit and the Prophet says he is commanded to submit, closely matching the source section's “only your Lord.”
luna: The section defines the Lord as owner of every thing; this verse says وَهُوَ رَبُّ كُلِّ شَىْءٍ and then identifies the return to Him.

luna: The command to set one’s face toward worship and call on God sincerely gives a concrete posture and act for the section’s exclusive Godward desire. | terra: Setting one's face at every place of worship and calling God with sincere religion turn bodily direction and invocation into a repeated exclusive practice.
luna: The verse commands calling on the Lord in fear and hope, a repeated formulation of the posture described in 21:90.
terra: The threatened magicians ask their Lord to pour out (أَفْرِغْ) patience and take them as submitters; the root's pouring sense serves steadfast, exclusively Godward endurance under pain.

luna: At Badr, the believers are told تُرِيدُونَ عَرَضَ ٱلدُّنْيَا while Allah wills the Hereafter; this makes the section's warning against a broad worldly desire explicit. | terra: “You desire the goods of the world, while God desires the Hereafter” directly opposes acquisition-minded desire to the divine direction a prophetic task requires.

terra: Family, acquired wealth, feared commercial loss, and pleasing homes must not become dearer than God, His Messenger, and striving in His way; the ayah tests worldly acquisition against directed exertion.

terra: When called to go forth in God's path, some grow heavy toward the earth and prefer worldly life to the Hereafter; downward attachment and refusal of effort directly reverse the command to rise and labor toward the Lord.

luna: The preceding verse shows the charity critics pleased when given a share and angry when not; 9:59 answers that appetite with contentment in God's allotment and desire for Allah. | terra: The critic of alms is pleased only when given a share and angry when not, embodying desire fixed on distribution; 9:59 replaces that stance with confidence in God's bounty and desire toward God.

luna: The section's root ر غ ب is used in إِنَّا إِلَى ٱللَّهِ رَٰغِبُونَ: in a dispute over charity allotments, the proper answer is to desire Allah and accept His and His Messenger's giving. | terra: Instead of making satisfaction depend on a share of alms, the speakers should trust what God and His Messenger give and say إِنَّا إِلَى ٱللَّهِ رَاغِبُونَ; the object of desire shifts from the allotment to God, its giver.
luna: The verse after the charity response in 9:59 specifies the recipients of alms, locating the promised allotment in an actual distribution.

terra: “Work” is followed by the assurance that God, His Messenger, and believers will see the work and that people will be returned to God; present labor is placed under its final divine destination.
luna: Allah is described as purchasing believers’ lives and property in exchange for the Garden; this concretely joins the Lord’s ownership, human effort, and abundant reward.

luna: The section names ر غ ب and ن ص ب; here soldiers must not prefer their own lives over the Messenger, and the verse names thirst, نَصَب, and hunger in service of God. | terra: This ayah joins both sides of the section's image: believers must not turn themselves away from the Messenger (يَرْغَبُوا۟ ... عَن), and every thirst, fatigue (نَصَبٌ), and step borne in God's path is credited as a righteous deed.

luna: The next verse records every small or large expense and every valley crossed for God's cause as a deed, showing effort directed to God and its recompense. | terra: No small or large expenditure and no valley crossed in the campaign goes unwritten; it continues 9:120's directed fatigue by showing each further act preserved for the best recompense.

luna: When harm is removed, the person continues as if he had never called Allah; this reverses the section's instruction to turn to the Lord after a difficulty or task has ended. | terra: A person in distress calls God lying, sitting, or standing, then passes on after relief as though never calling; temporary bodily orientation under need reverses the section's continuing cycle of devotion.
luna: In a storm at sea people call Allah sincerely, then the scene turns after rescue; this is a specific danger-and-relief setting for the change of orientation in 10:23.
luna: After being saved to land, they commit injustice; the post-rescue turn away from God reverses the section's call to turn to Him after a completed ordeal.
terra: The Prophet is commanded to set his face toward the religion uprightly and not be among the associators, expressing exclusive orientation as a sustained posture.

luna: Those who want worldly life and its adornment are paid for their deeds in this life but receive no share beyond it, a direct boundary on worldly-directed labor. | terra: Those who desire worldly life and its adornment are paid their works in it, so labor can receive its whole horizon from the wrong object of desire.

luna: The next verse states their Hereafter outcome and that their deeds have come to nothing, completing the warning in 11:15. | terra: For the world-seekers of 11:15 only fire remains in the Hereafter and their works become void, supplying the same boundary as the source section's warning about undirected fatigue.

terra: Shuayb describes reform as the work he seeks to do, says success comes only through God, and concludes عَلَيْهِ تَوَكَّلْتُ وَإِلَيْهِ أُنِيبُ; effort, enablement, and return have one source and direction.
terra: At the culmination of Joseph's long work and reunion, he names dominion and knowledge as his Lord's gifts, then asks the Creator to take him in submission and join him to the righteous.
terra: Patience is undertaken seeking the Lord's face and is joined to prayer, giving, and repelling evil with good; endurance and a chain of acts receive their direction from the Lord.
terra: God guides to Himself whoever turns back, a concise promise that Godward direction draws a corresponding gift of guidance.

terra: The Prophet is commanded to recite revelation and say that God alone is his Lord, on Him he relies, and to Him is his return; the repeated إِلَيْهِ gives the section's direction an explicit confessional form.
terra: Those who prefer worldly life to the Hereafter and obstruct God's way embody desire expanding toward the world until it also bends others' direction.

luna: The section's root ن ص ب for fatigue is reversed in the Garden: its people are not touched by نَصَب, so toil gives way to repose. | terra: Paradise's people are touched by no fatigue (نَصَبٌ) and will never be removed, setting a boundary to the section's present command of tiring, repeated service.

luna: The command وَٱعْبُدْ رَبَّكَ حَتَّىٰ يَأْتِيَكَ ٱلْيَقِينُ makes devotion to the Lord continue until certainty comes, giving the section's new-work cycle an endpoint. | terra: The command to worship one's Lord until certainty comes gives the section's tiring upright devotion its duration: renewed service continues until death.
luna: The section's dictionary branch for ر ب ب names blessing and goodness; this verse states that every نعمة people have is from Allah, clarifying the source of the gift they seek.
luna: After Allah removes harm, a group associates others with their Lord; the verse reverses the section's exclusive turn toward Him after a change of circumstance.
luna: The next ayah says they deny what they were given and enjoy themselves for a time, completing the reversal from gift to ingratitude in 16:54.

luna: The same source-section root ش ر ح is used in مَن شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا, an opening of the breast toward disbelief, the contrary of the Godward opening in 94:1. | terra: The one who willingly opens his breast to unbelief (شَرَحَ بِٱلْكُفْرِ صَدْرًا) gives the ش ر ح image the opposite content from a breast opened for prophetic, Godward work.
terra: Preferring worldly life over the Hereafter explains the sealing of hearts, showing how chosen direction can undo the opened, receptive breast.

luna: The verse contrasts a person who desires ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ and is given only what God wills with the section's desire aimed at the Lord; the outcome exposes the limit of seeking the immediate world. | terra: Whoever desires only the immediate life receives a measured portion and then Hell; it is a precise instance of wide desire being directed toward the nearer world, opposed by 17:19.

luna: The other side of 17:18 desires the Hereafter and سَعَىٰ لَهَا سَعْيَهَا while believing; it joins directed desire to purposeful effort as the section does. | terra: Whoever desires the Hereafter, strives for it with the striving due it, and believes has that striving gratefully received; desire's object determines the worth of labor.
terra: The Lord extends His gift (عَطَآءِ رَبِّكَ) to both groups, making Him the source even when human desires diverge and directly recalling the section's “abundant gift” sense of الرغيبة.
terra: The command to observe how divine gifts differ culminates in the greater degrees and favor of the Hereafter, completing 17:18-20's contrast between two directed desires.
luna: Those invoked besides God themselves seek access to their Lord, hope for His mercy, and fear His punishment; this explicitly describes desire directed toward the Lord with hope and fear.

luna: At sea, distress leaves people calling only Allah, but once He saves them to land they turn away; this makes the section's post-relief orientation a clear boundary. | terra: At sea, danger strips away every invoked object except God, but safe arrival on land is followed by turning away; the scene exposes an unstable, crisis-bound Godward direction.

luna: The Prophet is told to perform extra prayer at night in hope that his Lord will raise him to a praised station, joining night effort to hope in the Lord’s gift. | terra: The Prophet is commanded to keep an additional night vigil, with the hope that his Lord will raise him to a praised station; taxing worship, hoped-for divine gift, and rising are linked.

luna: The verse sets people who call their Lord morning and evening, seeking His face, against one who wants the adornment of worldly life and follows desire; this closely meets the section’s turn from broad worldly longing to the Lord. | terra: The Prophet must remain with those who call their Lord morning and evening desiring His face, and must not look past them seeking worldly adornment; Godward desire and worldward appetite are directly opposed.
luna: The parable begins with two men, one given two gardens; it is another concrete garden scene that frames the section’s lost-garden owners and their changed appeal to God.
luna: The garden owner boasts that he has more wealth and followers, supplying the worldly confidence that contrasts with the section’s later appeal to the Lord after loss.

luna: The boastful owner assumes that, if returned to his Lord, he will receive an even better return; this makes his expectation of worldly gain a false counterpart to the section’s humble hope in the Lord.
luna: The other man says Allah is his Lord and he associates no one with Him, giving a direct contrasting stance within the same garden story.
luna: The believing companion tells the owner to acknowledge Allah’s will and power when entering the garden, making the source of worldly provision explicit.
luna: The companion says his Lord may give him a better garden and send a calamity upon the other; this anticipates the section’s garden owners hoping their Lord will replace what they lost.
luna: The companion warns that the garden’s water could sink beyond recovery, naming the concrete limit on the owner’s apparent security.
luna: After his garden is destroyed, the owner regrets that he associated anyone with his Lord; it is a close parallel to the section’s owners turning toward their Lord after losing a garden.
luna: No faction can help the ruined owner against Allah, adding the collapse of worldly support to the garden-loss scene.
luna: The passage concludes that true protection belongs to Allah and that He gives the best reward and outcome, identifying the Lord as the lasting source of support.

luna: Wealth and children are called adornment of worldly life, while lasting good deeds are better with the Lord as reward and hope; this gives a precise world-versus-enduring-work boundary. | terra: Wealth and children are worldly adornment, while enduring good deeds are better with the Lord in reward and hope; what is acquired is contrasted with work whose value remains before its Giver.

luna: After the journey Moses says لَقَدْ لَقِينَا مِن سَفَرِنَا هَٰذَا نَصَبًا; this is the section's root ن ص ب in its fatigue sense, attached to purposeful travel. | terra: Moses names the fatigue (نَصَبًا) met on his journey; it is the same bodily weariness developed from ن ص ب, though here the ayah marks travel toward a human teacher rather than worship itself.

terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn says what his Lord has established him in is better than the offered payment and asks the people to help with strength; the barrier project begins by preferring divine provision and directing collective labor.

terra: Dhu al-Qarnayn directs a sequence of strenuous acts—bring iron, blow, bring molten copper to pour (أُفْرِغْ)—whose finished result he attributes to his Lord's mercy in 18:98; the ف ر غ form itself bears the separate “pour” sense.
terra: After the barrier-building work of 18:96-97 is complete, Dhu al-Qarnayn calls it a mercy from his Lord and points to his Lord's future promise, redirecting accomplishment away from himself.
terra: The question about the greatest losers in works prepares a direct case of effort whose direction makes it futile, specified in 18:104.

luna: The verse says some people’s effort is lost in worldly life although they think they are doing good, a direct counterpart to the section’s warning that exertion can be wasted if it lacks the right direction. | terra: Their striving goes astray in worldly life while they think they are doing well, a precise counterpart to exhausted work that never reaches its proper Lordward end.

luna: The following verse says their deeds carry no weight on the Day of Resurrection because they rejected their Lord’s signs and meeting Him, supplying the reason and outcome for the lost effort in 18:104.

luna: The verse says whoever hopes to meet his Lord should do righteous work and associate no one in worship with Him, joining effort, hope, and exclusive orientation. | terra: Whoever hopes to meet his Lord must do righteous work and admit no partner into the Lord's worship; hoped-for encounter, action, and exclusive direction are stated together.

luna: The section's root ر غ ب for turning desire away occurs in Abraham's father's question أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنْ ءَالِهَتِى; it is the opposite direction from the section's desire toward the Lord. | terra: Abraham's father asks أَرَاغِبٌ أَنتَ عَنْ ءَالِهَتِى, using رغبة with عَنْ for rejection; 19:48 then shows Abraham's positive direction toward his Lord.

luna: Abraham's immediate reply to his father is that he will ask his Lord to forgive him, continuing the exchange from rejection of the idols toward appeal to the Lord. | terra: Abraham answers his father's threat with peace and promises to ask his Lord's forgiveness; this begins the positive Lordward turn completed in 19:48.

luna: Abraham says he will separate from what they invoke besides Allah and call upon his Lord; this makes the turn away from idols in 19:46 a turn toward God. | terra: Abraham withdraws from his father's gods and says he will call upon his Lord, enacting the redirection that 19:46 frames with رَاغِبٌ ... عَنْ.
terra: The Lord of the heavens and earth is to be worshipped with steadfast perseverance in His worship, giving the section's repeated tiring service both its object and its sustaining command.
terra: “Go to Pharaoh” gives Moses the hard work for which he immediately asks his Lord to open his breast in 20:25; the link is the commission that makes the opening purposeful.

luna: Moses prays رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى before undertaking his mission; the opened breast equips someone for the next task. | terra: Moses answers the commission to Pharaoh by praying رَبِّ ٱشْرَحْ لِى صَدْرِى; opened breast, Lord, and readiness for a hard prophetic task meet as they do across 94:1 and 94:7-8.

luna: Moses follows the request in 20:25 with وَيَسِّرْ لِىٓ أَمْرِى, asking that his task be made easy; this continues the link between an opened breast and taking on work. | terra: Moses asks his Lord to ease his task after asking for an opened breast, connecting divine enlargement to the labor it enables rather than to rest for its own sake.

luna: The Prophet is told not to fix his eyes on worldly adornments given to others because his Lord’s provision is better and more lasting; this directly counters the section’s secondary image of broad desire for the world.

luna: The next command is to keep the family at prayer and be patient in it, since Allah provides; it joins sustained effort in worship to provision from the Lord. | terra: The Prophet must command his household to pray and persevere in it; God asks no provision from them but provides for them, sharply ordering exertion, desire, and gift around the Lord.

luna: This is the prayer immediately before the household described in 21:90: Zakariya asks his Lord not to leave him alone, making the next verse's hopeful and fearful calling concrete. | terra: Zechariah's “My Lord, do not leave me alone” supplies the concrete Godward request answered in 21:90, where his household's prayer is characterized as hope and fear.

luna: The section's root ر غ ب appears in رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا: Zakariya's household hastens to good deeds and calls on God with hope and fear, joining exertion to directed prayer. | terra: God answers Zechariah, grants John, and repairs his wife because the household hastened in good works and called on Him رَغَبًا وَرَهَبًا; hopeful desire is joined to action, fear, humility, and divine gift.
luna: During the pilgrimage, people are to witness benefits and mention Allah’s name over the livestock He provided; it joins completed ritual, remembrance, and provision from God.
luna: The next verse tells pilgrims to complete their rites, fulfill their vows, and circumambulate the Ancient House, extending the Hajj scene around the remembrance named in 22:28.
luna: For every community a rite is appointed so they mention Allah’s name over the livestock He provided; the verse connects worship to gifts from the one God.
luna: The sacrificial camels are made among God’s signs, and His name is mentioned over them; it gives a concrete form to sacrifice directed to the Lord.

luna: The next verse says neither meat nor blood reaches Allah, but God-consciousness does; it clarifies that sacrifice’s Godward intention, not its material object, is what matters. | terra: Sacrificial meat and blood do not reach God, but piety does; the animals were subjected so believers may magnify Him, clarifying that an act's Godward direction lies in its intention rather than its material output.
terra: Believers are commanded to bow, prostrate, worship their Lord, and do good so that they may prosper; bodily worship and useful work lead directly into 22:78's striving for God.

terra: Believers are commanded to strive for God with the striving due Him, then establish prayer, give alms, and hold fast to Him; exhausting service is explicitly directed and sustained by their Protector.

luna: Commerce and sale do not distract these people from Allah's remembrance, prayer, and giving; this concretizes the section's return to the Lord amid a long day's work. | terra: Trade and sale do not distract these people from God's remembrance, prayer, and alms, so ordinary work remains ordered around worship rather than widening desire toward acquisition.
terra: The servants of the Merciful spend the night before their Lord prostrating and standing, making strenuous uprightness an enacted relation to the Lord.

terra: God is the one who sees the Prophet when he rises; in the surrounding appeal to trust the Mighty and Merciful, this makes prophetic rising accountable to the Lord, though the precise act of rising is not specified in the ayah.
terra: Solomon responds to a bestowed ability by asking his Lord to enable gratitude, righteous work pleasing to Him, and entry into His mercy; gift, work, and desire all return to the Giver.
terra: Once the throne is set before Solomon, he immediately names the achievement “from my Lord's favor” and sees it as a test of gratitude, turning a completed feat back toward its Giver.

terra: The heart of Moses' mother becomes فَارِغًا and is then bound firm by God; this distinct “empty” sense of ف ر غ shows that vacancy alone is unstable until the heart is given a sustaining direction.

terra: Moses first completes the concrete labor of watering for the two women, then withdraws and addresses his Lord as wholly needy for whatever good He sends; it enacts work followed immediately by Godward desire and provision.
terra: Whatever people are given is temporary worldly enjoyment and adornment, while what is with God is better and more lasting; gift is distinguished from its enduring source.

luna: The section's root ن ص ب also appears in نَصِيبَكَ, one's share; this verse sets seeking the Hereafter beside not forgetting one's worldly share and doing good as Allah has done good. | terra: Qarun is told to seek the lasting abode with what God has given him, retain his proper worldly share, and do good as God did good to him; divine gift is deliberately redirected into further good work.
terra: Those desiring worldly life wish for wealth like Qarun's when he appears in his adornment, a concrete scene of the acquisition-focused رغبة described in the source dictionary.

terra: Those given knowledge answer the wishers of 28:79 that God's reward is better for the believing righteous, but attained by the patient; gift, labor, and endurance are redirected beyond Qarun's display.
luna: People aboard a ship call Allah sincerely, then associate others when He brings them safely to land; the reversal opposes the section's exclusive desire toward the Lord.
terra: Those who exert themselves “for Us” are promised guidance into God's ways; strenuous action is qualified by its recipient and answered with divine guidance.
terra: The command to set one's face toward the religion uprightly makes directedness itself the governing image of faithful action.
terra: People call their Lord while turning to Him under harm, yet after tasting mercy some associate partners; the change of circumstance reveals a direction that does not endure.
terra: Giving relatives, the needy, and the traveler their due is declared best for those who desire God's face; active generosity becomes the form taken by Godward desire.
terra: Worldly lending meant to increase through people's wealth is set against alms given desiring God's face; the ayah tests desire by both its direction and the kind of increase sought.
terra: The believer must follow the path of one who turns to God, and all will return to Him; chosen present direction is placed inside the unavoidable final return.
terra: One who submits his face to God while doing good has grasped the firmest handhold, and the outcome of all matters is to God; present action and final direction coincide.

luna: People leave their beds to call their Lord in fear and hope and spend from what He provided; this brings rising, exertion, directed prayer, and divine provision into one image. | terra: Their sides leave their beds as they call upon their Lord in fear and hope, a bodily rising into the same رغبا ورهبا orientation expressed in 21:90.
luna: The next verse says no soul knows what comfort has been hidden for these workers as recompense for their deeds, connecting their effort to an abundant gift from God.
terra: ٱعْمَلُوٓا۟ ءَالَ دَاوُۥدَ شُكْرًا commands David's household to turn the gifts just described into work as gratitude, showing divine bounty generating further directed labor.

luna: Those who recite the Book, establish prayer, and spend from God’s provision hope for a trade that will never fail, joining effort and worship to a lasting return. | terra: Reciting God's book, establishing prayer, and spending from His provision are people’s hope for a trade that will never perish; work and commerce are redirected toward lasting divine return.
luna: The next verse says God will pay their wages in full and increase them from His bounty, specifying the gift behind their hoped-for return.

luna: Here too the Garden's people say fatigue نَصَب does not touch them; the repeated absence of toil sharpens the section's picture of exertion in this life. | terra: The people settled in the lasting abode praise God because neither fatigue (نَصَبٌ) nor weariness touches them there; directed labor belongs to the journey, not its completed reward.
terra: Abraham says, “I am going to my Lord; He will guide me,” making movement toward the Lord both an intentional departure and an expectation of divine provision.
terra: Job calls his Lord when afflicted with نُصْبٍ and torment; the fatigue root developed in the section appears inside a concrete act of Godward appeal.

luna: The person calls his Lord, دَعَا رَبَّهُ مُنِيبًا إِلَيْهِ, but forgets that prayer when given a blessing; the section's direction toward the Lord is set against forgetting Him after receiving good. | terra: When harm touches a person he calls his Lord turning to Him, but after divine favor he forgets and assigns rivals; gift becomes the occasion for reversed desire rather than renewed service.
terra: The night devotee prostrates and stands, fears the Hereafter, and hopes for his Lord's mercy; bodily standing is given the paired directions of fear and hope, unlike heedless toil.
terra: The Prophet says he is commanded to worship God with religion made sincere for Him, a direct statement of the exclusive direction expressed by the source section's fronted “to your Lord.”
terra: The Prophet declares that God is the one he worships, making his devotion sincere for Him; the fronted object gives the same exclusive force as the section's وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ.
terra: Those who avoid serving false powers and turn to God receive good news, giving the positive redirection that contrasts with the erected cult objects condemned in 5:90.

luna: This repeats the section's ش ر ح / breast image as a chest Allah opens to Islam, contrasting inner light with mere worldly expansiveness. | terra: A breast God has opened to Islam places its possessor upon light from his Lord; this supplies the Godward content of the opened breast recalled in the section.

luna: The verse commands people to turn toward their Lord and submit to Him, directly paralleling the section’s direction إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ. | terra: أَنِيبُوا۟ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكُمْ وَأَسْلِمُوا۟ لَهُ commands an intentional turn to the Lord followed by submission before judgment arrives, a direct parallel to purposeful redirection after one phase ends.
terra: Believers are commanded to call upon God with religion sincere for Him even when unbelievers dislike it, making exclusive Godward appeal a deliberate stance under opposition.
terra: The Prophet is told to persevere because God's promise is true, seek forgiveness, and glorify his Lord evening and morning; endurance opens into a recurring cycle of Lordward acts.
terra: Because the Living One alone is God, people are commanded to call upon Him sincerely and praise the Lord of the worlds; exclusive address and lordship are joined explicitly.
luna: The Prophet is told to become upright toward God and seek His forgiveness; it joins an upright stance with a directed return to Him.
terra: God chooses whom He wills and guides to Himself whoever turns back, so deliberate reorientation toward Him is answered by divine guidance.

luna: The verse contrasts one who wants the harvest of the Hereafter, whose yield God increases, with one who wants the harvest of this world; it joins work and the direction of desire. | terra: One who desires the harvest of the Hereafter receives increase, while one who desires the worldly harvest receives some of it but no share beyond; the direction of desire governs both work's yield and its permanence.

terra: Whatever people are given is temporary worldly enjoyment, while what is with God is better and lasting for believers who rely on their Lord; the Giver and the gift are put in their proper order.
terra: Those who respond to their Lord establish prayer and conduct affairs by consultation while spending from His provision, turning divine response and gift into an ongoing field of work.
terra: At full maturity, the person asks his Lord for power to thank Him for His favor and to do righteous work pleasing to Him; received bounty becomes fresh, expressly directed labor.
terra: The Prophet's companions are seen bowing and prostrating while seeking bounty and pleasure from God, joining strenuous worship to the desire for divine gift.
luna: The righteous are described as sleeping little at night; this is another concrete night-devotion scene beside the section’s command to rise at night.
luna: The same people seek forgiveness before dawn, completing the night-to-day devotion scene introduced in 51:17.

luna: The command فَفِرُّوا إِلَى ٱللَّهِ directly names movement toward God, paralleling the section’s direction إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ. | terra: فَفِرُّوٓا۟ إِلَى ٱللَّهِ makes movement toward God an urgent command from the Messenger, a vivid nonlexical counterpart to directing all رغبة to the Lord.
luna: The next verse forbids setting another deity alongside Allah, making the exclusivity of fleeing toward Him explicit.
terra: The Prophet is told to endure his Lord's judgment and glorify Him when he rises (حِينَ تَقُومُ), joining rising, patience, and praise under the Lord's gaze.
terra: The Prophet is to glorify God during the night and as the stars retreat, continuing 52:48's command to praise when rising into a repeated daily rhythm.

luna: The person who turns away from God's remembrance and wants only worldly life, لَمْ يُرِدْ إِلَّا ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا, embodies the opposite stance to turning desire toward the Lord. | terra: The Prophet must turn away from one who turns from God's remembrance and desires only worldly life, combining wrong desire with an enacted turning away from the divine reminder.
luna: The next verse says the Lord knows best who has strayed from His way and who is guided, supplying the divine judgment on the worldly preference described in 53:29.
terra: A person has only what he strives for; 53:40-42 continue from visible effort and full recompense to the declaration that the endpoint is the Lord.
terra: Human striving will be seen, so the labor named in 53:39 is purposeful and accountable on its way to the Lord's endpoint in 53:42.
terra: The striving of 53:39 will receive the fullest repayment before 53:42 names the Lord as the final end, connecting sustained work with its divine issue.

luna: The section names the root ر ب ب and says all paths end with the Lord; وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ states that destination directly. | terra: وَأَنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلْمُنتَهَىٰ makes the Lord the endpoint with the same fronted directional phrase that the section hears in وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ.
luna: Before the address in 55:31, this verse says all in the heavens and earth ask God and He is each day in an affair, adding the ongoing divine activity behind the section’s use of farag for God.

luna: The section's root ف ر غ shifts subject: God says سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ to the two weighty communities, a warning of His focused attention rather than a human being free to begin another task. | terra: سَنَفْرُغُ لَكُمْ uses the source root ف ر غ of God turning intentionally to the two weighty communities; it confirms the section's developed sense that “becoming free” can mean a deliberate new address.

terra: Worldly life is play, adornment, boasting, and rivalry in wealth and children whose growth withers, while the Hereafter holds punishment or divine forgiveness and pleasure; acquisitive effort is measured by what remains.

terra: Monasticism was innovated while seeking God's pleasure, yet was not observed as it should have been; the ayah sets a boundary showing that a claimed Godward aim does not excuse a form of labor not faithfully kept.
terra: The poor emigrants lose homes and wealth while seeking bounty and pleasure from God and supporting His cause, a concrete case of exhausting labor directed beyond worldly acquisition.
terra: Abraham and his companions say to God, “upon You we rely, to You we turn, and to You is the destination”; trust, present reorientation, and final arrival are all exclusively Godward.

luna: The address offers a trade that saves from painful punishment, setting up the section’s image of effort yielding a gift from God. | terra: God offers a “trade” that saves from punishment, deliberately recasting the world of acquisition as an exchange whose direction and gain are divine.

luna: That trade is specified as faith and striving in Allah’s cause with wealth and lives, making exertion explicitly God-directed. | terra: The saving trade consists of faith and striving with wealth and lives in God's way, making costly work the concrete expression of the desire introduced in 61:10.
luna: The following verse names forgiveness and Gardens as the return for that striving, completing the passage’s divine reward.

luna: This is the preceding stage of the Friday sequence completed in 62:10: leave trade when the call comes and hasten to Allah's remembrance before spreading out again. | terra: The call to Friday prayer requires leaving trade and hastening to God's remembrance; together with 62:10 it forms the reverse half of the section's cycle between labor and worship.

luna: The section's finish-then-act cycle is staged after Friday prayer: when it ends, spread through the land, seek Allah's bounty, and remember Him much. | terra: When Friday prayer is finished, believers disperse through the earth seeking God's bounty while remembering Him much, showing that transition into worldly work can itself stay oriented to the Giver.

terra: When trade or amusement appears, people leave the Prophet standing; the ayah declares what is with God better and God the best provider, exposing the very worldward diversion that 62:9-10's work-worship cycle must govern.
terra: Believers are warned not to let wealth and children distract them from God's remembrance, a specific boundary keeping ordinary concerns inside the cycle of Godward attention.
luna: The section's garden owners are introduced as people tested through a garden; this is the scene whose loss later turns them toward their Lord in 68:32.
luna: Before the loss, the owners resolve not to make an exception; that presumption contrasts with their later hope in the Lord's replacement in 68:32.
luna: The garden's destruction comes as a visitation from their Lord while they sleep, adding divine ownership and provision to the scene that ends in their appeal.
luna: The garden is left like a harvested field; this is the concrete loss behind the owners' later blame and hope for a better replacement.
luna: The owners tell each other to go early to their crop if they intend to harvest it, supplying the labor and worldly aim behind the lost-garden scene.
luna: On the way they resolve that no needy person should enter; this selfish plan contrasts with their later appeal to the Lord after the garden is gone.

luna: One brother asks why they did not glorify God, identifying the neglected Godward response that frames their later confession and desire toward the Lord. | terra: The most balanced garden owner recalls that he had urged the others to glorify God; this is the first explicit summons away from acquisitive plotting and toward the Lord before 68:29-32.

luna: After the garden is lost they say سُبْحَٰنَ رَبِّنَا and admit wrongdoing; the scene moves from self-directed harvest to recognition of their Lord. | terra: Before declaring their desire toward their Lord in 68:32, the garden owners glorify their Lord and admit wrongdoing, showing the reorientation beginning in confession.

luna: This is the mutual reproach explicitly mentioned in the section, immediately before the owners turn to their Lord in 68:32. | terra: The garden owners first turn toward one another in blame, then in 68:32 turn their hope toward their Lord; the two directions expose the change produced by repentance.

luna: Their next words confess that they had transgressed; that admission makes their appeal for a better gift from their Lord in 68:32 a changed stance. | terra: Their admission that they transgressed clears the way for 68:32's hope in a better replacement from their Lord, so the desired gift follows moral recognition rather than mere loss.

luna: The section names the root ر غ ب for desire toward the Lord; after their garden is lost, its owners say إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَٰغِبُونَ and hope He will replace it with something better. | terra: After the garden is lost, its owners hope their Lord will replace it with something better and say إِنَّا إِلَىٰ رَبِّنَا رَاغِبُونَ; desire, direction, Lord, and hoped-for abundant gift all coincide.
luna: The garden episode closes by contrasting punishment in this life with the greater punishment of the Hereafter, widening the owners' lost worldly provision into an afterlife boundary.

terra: On resurrection they rush from graves as though racing toward an erected target (نُصُبٍ); the source dictionary's “setting upright” sense appears as a false or merely apparent destination rather than upright service to the Lord.

terra: When God's servant stands calling upon Him, the crowd nearly masses around him; standing and Godward invocation coincide in a scene especially close to “rise, exert yourself, and desire your Lord.”

luna: The command قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ calls the Prophet to rise for night worship, a concrete instance of the section's instruction to get up and exert oneself. | terra: قُمِ ٱلَّيْلَ commands the same Prophet to rise for demanding night worship; 73:7-8 place this rising beside daytime occupation and total direction to the Lord.

luna: This neighbor names the day as a long occupation, which explains the section's pairing of daytime work with night devotion and turning to the Lord in 73:8. | terra: The Prophet's long daytime engagement (سَبْحًا طَوِيلًا) supplies the work phase of the cycle whose Godward phase is stated in 73:8.

luna: After the long daytime occupation of 73:7, the Prophet is told to remember his Lord's name and تَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ, devote himself wholly to Him, matching the section's redirection after work. | terra: Remembering the Lord's name and devoting oneself wholly to Him (تَبَتَّلْ إِلَيْهِ تَبْتِيلًا) is a close nonlexical formulation of the source section's exclusive وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَب.
terra: The Lord of east and west alone is God, so the Prophet is to take Him as trustee; this grounds 73:8's total self-devotion in exclusive lordship.

terra: God knows the Prophet and his companions stand through measured portions of the night, then mentions travelers seeking His bounty and fighters in His way; worship, taxing activity, and divine provision remain one directed cycle.

luna: The Prophet is commanded قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ, rise and warn; it is one of the section's own examples of rising into a new task. | terra: The Prophet is commanded قُمْ فَأَنذِرْ, a direct parallel to rising into purposeful labor in 94:7; 74:3 and 74:7 then fix that labor's direction upon his Lord.

luna: The next command in that address is ورَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ, to magnify the Lord, matching the section's directed stance after rising. | terra: وَرَبَّكَ فَكَبِّرْ fronts “your Lord” before the command, matching the exclusive emphasis of the source section's وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ and supplying the next Godward act after 74:2's rising.

luna: The same address ends this command sequence with وَلِرَبِّكَ فَٱصْبِرْ, be patient for your Lord; the action and its purpose are joined as in the section. | terra: وَلِرَبِّكَ فَٱصْبِرْ makes the Lord the expressly fronted purpose of sustained endurance, so the standing work begun in 74:2 is not directionless strain.

luna: The address says people love ٱلْعَاجِلَةَ, a specific counter-direction to the section's desire toward the Lord. | terra: Loving the immediate life states the attraction that pulls desire away from its proper Lordward direction.

luna: The next ayah adds that they leave the Hereafter, completing the immediate-life contrast of 75:20. | terra: Neglecting the Hereafter is the inseparable other side of 75:20's love of the immediate, exposing what world-directed desire leaves behind.
luna: The people feed the needy, orphan, and captive; 76:9 explains that this concrete act is done only for Allah’s face, giving directed effort an example.

luna: They say إِنَّمَا نُطْعِمُكُمْ لِوَجْهِ ٱللَّهِ and seek no reward or thanks, an explicit case of action oriented to God rather than human return. | terra: The feeders say they act only for God's face and desire no repayment or thanks from people; a concrete service is directed beyond every immediate human return.
luna: They explain the motive in 76:9 by saying they fear a day from their Lord, adding the accountability that guides their work.
luna: The next verse says Allah protects them from that day’s evil, the divine care that answers their God-directed effort.
luna: The passage concludes that Allah rewards their patience with a Garden and silk, showing the gift sought from the Lord after sustained effort.
terra: The Prophet must remember his Lord's name morning and evening, establishing the daily recurrence within which 76:26 places prolonged night worship.
terra: Night prostration and long glorification continue the morning-evening remembrance of 76:25, giving sustained duration to the command to labor toward the Lord.
terra: Those people love the immediate life and leave behind them a weighty day, so present preference evades rather than removes the final divine encounter.

luna: This person prefers worldly life, وَءَاثَرَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا, reversing the section's direction toward the Lord. | terra: Preferring worldly life is the decisive orientation of the transgressor; 79:40-41 oppose it with fear of standing before the Lord and restraint of desire.
luna: This neighbor gives the consequence of preferring worldly life: the blazing fire is the refuge.

luna: The counterpart fears standing before his Lord and restrains the soul from desire, وَنَهَى ٱلنَّفْسَ عَنِ ٱلْهَوَىٰ; it concretely joins reverence for the Lord to disciplining desire. | terra: Fear of standing before one's Lord restrains the soul from caprice, making the final standing before God govern desire and conduct now.

luna: This neighbor completes the contrast by naming the Garden as the refuge of the one who restrained desire before his Lord. | terra: Paradise becomes the dwelling of the person in 79:40, completing the reversal of 79:38's preference for worldly life.
luna: After describing a sealed drink for the righteous, the verse says to let those who compete compete for it, redirecting aspiration toward an abundant divine gift.

luna: The section's image of effort directed toward the Lord is stated as كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ; the person strives toward his Lord and will meet Him. | terra: Every human being is laboring painfully toward the Lord (كَادِحٌ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ) and will meet Him, making explicit both the exertion and the final direction that 94:7-8 bind together.
terra: Remembering the name of one's Lord and praying supplies the positive Godward acts immediately before 87:16 exposes preference for worldly life.

luna: The verse names preferring ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا, the opposite of the section's instruction to direct desire to the Lord. | terra: بَلْ تُؤْثِرُونَ ٱلْحَيَوٰةَ ٱلدُّنْيَا states the worldly preference that the source's dictionary question attributes to an expansive desire toward acquisition.

luna: Its neighbor says the Hereafter is better and more enduring, completing the contrast to preferring worldly life in 87:16. | terra: The Hereafter is better and more lasting, naming the enduring alternative to 87:16's nearer-life preference and correcting desire's scale.

luna: The section itself cites عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ, faces working and weary on the Day of Judgment; their exhausting labor is the image's contrast to effort deliberately turned toward the Lord. | terra: عَامِلَةٌ نَّاصِبَةٌ presents laboring, exhausted faces whose next destination is the blazing fire in 88:4; it is the section's tiring exertion stripped of its saving Godward direction.
terra: Entering the intensely hot fire supplies the outcome of the exhausted labor in 88:3 and makes its opposition to labor directed toward the Lord concrete.

luna: The tranquil soul is called to return to its Lord, satisfied and accepted; this adds a personal return and satisfaction to the section’s claim that the destination is the Lord. | terra: The tranquil soul is commanded to return to its Lord, satisfied and pleasing; the final Godward turn fulfills directed desire in mutual contentment.
terra: “Your striving is diverse” states the problem at the heart of the section: exertion takes its value from the direction disclosed in the alternatives of 92:5-10.
terra: The person who gives and remains mindful begins the positive course of striving whose outcome is ease in 92:7.
terra: Affirming the best promise supplies the believed destination that distinguishes the giver's striving before 92:7 promises facilitation toward ease.
terra: God will ease the giver and believer toward ease, linking the direction of effort in 92:5-6 with the ease that God provides.
terra: The one who withholds and regards himself self-sufficient begins the opposite course of striving, reversing both giving and dependence upon the Lord.
terra: Denying the best promise supplies the wrong destination behind the withholding and self-sufficiency of 92:8.
terra: God will ease that person toward hardship, making the trajectory of misdirected effort the inverse of the ease promised in 92:7.
luna: The person gives his wealth to purify himself; 92:20 completes the motive as seeking his Lord’s face, paralleling effort aimed at God.
luna: This giving repays no favor from anyone, removing human reciprocity before the next verse names the Lord as its aim.

luna: The section’s desire directed to the Lord is stated as إِلَّا ٱبْتِغَاءَ وَجْهِ رَبِّهِ ٱلْأَعْلَىٰ, a motive seeking the Lord’s face. | terra: The giver acts only in seeking the face of his Lord Most High, an exclusivity reinforced by 92:19's denial that he is merely repaying another person's favor.
luna: The final verse says this giver will be satisfied, completing the passage’s account of Godward work and its hoped-for outcome.

luna: The Lord's abundant giving, named in the section's dictionary gloss for ر غ ب, has a direct promise here: وَلَسَوْفَ يُعْطِيكَ رَبُّكَ فَتَرْضَىٰ. | terra: The Prophet is promised that his Lord will give until he is satisfied; the Lord as giver of ample bounty concretely fills out the section's dictionary link between رغبة, gift, and Rabb.

luna: The section's root ر ب ب is joined to blessing in its dictionary gloss; this verse tells the Prophet to speak of the favor of his Lord, بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ. | terra: وَأَمَّا بِنِعْمَةِ رَبِّكَ فَحَدِّثْ joins “your Lord” directly to His favor and makes that favor occasion a new command, matching the section's developed ر ب ب sense of blessing and beneficence.
terra: Human beings transgress when they regard themselves as self-sufficient; 96:8 answers this false independence with the unavoidable return to the Lord.
terra: Seeing oneself free of need is the inner stance opposed to وَإِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ فَٱرْغَب, since it imagines no gift or direction beyond the self; 96:8 corrects it.

luna: The section's claim that return is to the Lord is directly phrased إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ. | terra: إِنَّ إِلَىٰ رَبِّكَ ٱلرُّجْعَىٰ answers the self-sufficiency of 96:6-7: however a person directs desire now, the return is exclusively to the Lord.
terra: People were commanded only to worship God sincerely and uprightly, establish prayer, and give alms; exclusive orientation issues in repeated concrete acts.

luna: The command فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَٱنْحَرْ directs both prayer and sacrifice to the Lord, giving a concrete form to the section's exclusive orientation. | terra: فَصَلِّ لِرَبِّكَ وَٱنْحَرْ gives the Prophet two strenuous acts expressly “for your Lord,” matching the command pattern and exclusive direction developed from 94:7-8.
terra: The coming of God's victory marks the completed achievement that triggers the command to glorify and seek forgiveness in 110:3; its relevance depends on that continuation.
terra: Seeing people enter God's religion in crowds supplies the visible fruition of the prophetic task before 110:3 orders a fresh turn to praise and repentance.

luna: After help and victory arrive, the Prophet is told to glorify his Lord with praise and seek forgiveness; a completed mission turns directly into Godward action. | terra: When victory and the people's entry have arrived in 110:1-2, the Prophet is told to glorify his Lord and seek His forgiveness, an exact structural parallel to a completed charge opening into fresh devotion.
